name: Fuel Delivery (low-pressure supply to the DI pump)
description: Cell → pre-filter → lift pump → surge tank → twin feed pumps → 10-micron filter → bypass regulator (short-loop return at the tank, ~72 psi) → single -8 feed line under the passenger-side floor → engine-bay dry break → DI high-pressure pump inlet (engine system).

components.name: Factory LT fuel delivery (reference: returnless, PWM-controlled)
components.description: The 6th-gen Camaro uses an in-tank pump module with a remote fuel pump control module (FPCM) commanded by the ECM: returnless, variable pressure (~58 psi idle/cruise, ~72 psi WOT per EngineLabs; ICT Billet states 5 bar / 72 psi). The low-pressure supply feeds the engine-driven DI high-pressure pump (engine system). On the race car the factory tank/module is removed and replaced with the cell + surge tank system below, regulated to a constant ~72 psi.
components.location: Factory saddle tank under the rear seat (removed).

factory.name: GM in-tank fuel pump module + FPCM (returnless)
factory.notes: If the factory ECM stays, it expects to command the FPCM; with a mechanical return-style regulator, set the ECM to a fixed low-side pressure or retain the low-side pressure sensor per tuner.

specs.Low-side pressure: ~58 psi idle/cruise, ~72 psi WOT (factory variable); race: constant ~72 psi (500 kPa)

installNotes: Remove factory tank, module, EVAP canister and lines during strip (phase 1).
Tuner must reconfigure low-side fuel pressure control/DTCs.

components.name: Lift (transfer) pump
